checks.name: scope-boundary
checks.summary: Scope boundary for V2-085, recorded against base commit b0b9ffef8c628f8091e5dbfdbedf88736144a62c on branch v2-task/V2-085, BEFORE any source file was edited: this record's first commit contains rows 1-5 and the A1/A2 baseline, and internal/application/service.go was still byte-identical to the base at that commit (verified by git status --porcelain showing only .agents/v2/evidence paths). ROW 1 -- what this task makes true: an emergency stop now stops planning and preparation. Service.Plan and Service.Prepare each evaluate exactly one domain.Permit of kind domain.PermitClaim against a domain.ControlTarget and a control revision resolved INSIDE the same transaction from the Requirement's own Repository link and domain.EffectiveControl, so the set of control modes under which a caller can create an Increment or move one to ready shrinks from all seven to exactly two (allow, pause-intake). The seven-mode outcome for each of the two commands is asserted rather than logged, cross-checked in the same run against the package's permitAllowedTable mirror and against Capture's measured intake behaviour. ROW 2 -- what it deliberately does not do: internal/domain is byte-unchanged (no PermitKind, no ControlMode, no RequirementStatus, no IncrementStatus, no allowed() list change); no field is added to PlanRequest or PlanResponse or PrepareRequest or PrepareResponse, so contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is byte-unchanged and contracts_changed is empty; nothing is passed to domain.EffectFromPermit and no OutboxItem is staged, because domain.PermitKind.SideEffect() is false for claim and the allow-only closure in EffectFromPermit would wrongly deny both commands under pause-intake; the eight-kind stop matrix (internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go) and docs/product/definition.md are byte-unchanged; no route, no read model field, no owner-console control, no port, no stored field, no document kind and no index is added; the success path under allow is byte-identical. ROW 3 -- what it records but does not fix: (a) Orchestrator.RunFakeJourney reaches Plan and Prepare through a caller the component fabricates for itself (internal/runner/orchestrator.go, application.Caller{Role: RoleOwner, Subject: runner-local-owner}), which is V2-086's defect and is recorded here, not fixed -- internal/runner/** is prohibited and that fixture engages no Control Intent, so this task's guard cannot reach it; (b) the in-memory adapter never calls quota.Counter.TrueUp, so quota.ReadTransactionUsage admits only four READ transactions per budget day -- V2-087's defect, worked around in the new test by reading the store directly rather than through Service, never by weakening an assertion; (c) internal/store/firestore's suite prints ok while producing 49 --- SKIP lines with no emulator (measured: 49), so that package's run measured nothing about this change and is recorded as such under gate rule G7 rather than counted as a pass. ROW 4 -- what only a later task can establish: neither command has an HTTP route, so no live HTTP or dogfood observation of the new refusal is possible here; who may call Plan and Prepare, and whether they should be reachable at all, is V2-086's question. ROW 5 -- this task passes no release gate on its own: exactly one evidence record is issued, release_eligible is false, no capability id is cited, contracts/release-contract/** is untouched, .agents/v2/evidence/V2-022-release-live-dogfood.json is untouched, and no release BundleDigest moves.

checks.name: a2-defect-reproduced-before-repair
checks.summary: A2 MEASURED, by me, before writing any repair. The scenario the Work Order specifies -- an effective control mode of emergency-stop engaged on a ScopeInstallation Control Intent, then Service.Plan and then Service.Prepare -- is exactly what the pre-existing V2-082 probe drives, so it was executed rather than restated. VERBATIM verdict, the log line and the PASS line: '    framing_test.go:610: A6 FINDING (recorded, not fixed; V2-085 owns the repair): under an effective control mode of emergency-stop, Plan err=<nil> (canonical Requirement state moved: true) and Prepare err=<nil> (canonical Increment state moved to ready: true), while Service.StartFraming is denied with control policy denies operation. Plan and Prepare evaluate no domain.Permit at all, so a stop mode does not reach them; StartFraming evaluates domain.Permit with Kind claim and is therefore denied by every stop mode. internal/application/service.go is prohibited to V2-082, so this is escalated rather than changed.' then '--- PASS: TestPlanAndPrepareAreMeasuredUnderEmergencyStop (0.00s)' then 'ok  	github.com/takushi/agentic-loop-foundation/v2/internal/application	1.011s'. BEFORE ROW of the before/after table: under emergency-stop, Plan returns error nil, the parent Requirement's canonical state MOVED (a new Increment id appended and Version incremented), Prepare returns error nil, and the Increment REACHED domain.IncrementReady -- the only status Claim accepts. Service.StartFraming, which does evaluate domain.Permit with kind claim, was denied with 'control policy denies operation' in the same run, which is the control against which the defect is read. The probe's own line number was re-measured: the function is at internal/application/framing_test.go:565 (AGREES with the Work Order) and the log call is at :610 (AGREES).
